title: General work product
description: Default rubric for any deliverable: does it meet what was asked, is that proven, and is it honest about what is not.

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria are met
criteria.ask: Take each acceptance criterion defined before the work started. Is every one observably true now?
criteria.evidence: A checklist of the original criteria, each with the command output, file or behavior that shows it holds.

criteria.title: Verified, not asserted
criteria.ask: Did you run the project's own checks and exercise the changed behavior for real, rather than reasoning that it should work?
criteria.evidence: Commands run with their actual result (pass/fail counts), plus a manual or browser check of the changed behavior.

criteria.title: Nothing else broke
criteria.ask: What could this change have broken? Did you look there?
criteria.evidence: The full gate (typecheck, lint, tests, build) result and the neighboring behavior you re-checked.

criteria.title: Scope respected
criteria.ask: Does the diff contain only what the task needs? Was anything unrequested changed, deleted or installed?
criteria.evidence: The list of changed files, each tied to a requirement.

criteria.title: As simple as it can be
criteria.ask: Is there dead code, a needless abstraction, a duplicated helper or a clever trick a maintainer would have to decode?
criteria.evidence: What you removed or deliberately kept, and why.

criteria.title: Honest about gaps
criteria.ask: Does the report state what was not verified, what is still risky and what was deferred?
criteria.evidence: The residual-risks list as written in the report.

criteria.title: Useful next step
criteria.ask: Can the reader act on the result without asking you anything?
